# ${plugin_name} Repository Rules

This file is generated by `/roa-base:setup ${plugin_name}` and should be reviewed by the owning team before committing.

## ROA UI Defaults

- Use the target repository's existing Maven build and test workflow before introducing new tools or commands.
- Prefer the Maven Wrapper (`./mvnw` or `mvnw.cmd`) when the repository provides one.
- Follow the repository's existing ROA test structure, lifecycle, services, components, elements, models, and conventions unless they conflict with installed ROA guidance.
- Use Pandora metadata when exact `io.cyborgcode.roa.*` APIs, annotations, methods, overloads, component types, or available options are uncertain. Do not guess framework usage.
- Consult AI Teacher before generating new Java code when relevant lessons are available.
- Derive UI behavior from verified application evidence. Inspect the actual application, DOM, browser state, and network activity when needed; do not invent selectors, elements, synchronization behavior, or user flows.
- Prefer ROA component abstractions, element enums, typed services, insertion models, table abstractions, and synchronization mechanisms over raw Selenium interactions or ad hoc waits.
- Keep selectors and synchronization outside test bodies and centralized in the appropriate ROA element/component abstractions.
- Prefer deterministic synchronization over arbitrary sleeps or timing assumptions.
- Reuse suitable existing project components, services, models, and flows before creating new abstractions.
- Validate the smallest meaningful scope for the change and do not bypass, weaken, disable, or hide failing tests.
- Keep project-specific deviations or additional repository constraints explicit rather than silently diverging from ROA conventions.
